title: Redundant `lastProgressPublishedAt === 0` disjunct in queueProgress throttle gate
description: The first-publish special-case `state.lastProgressPublishedAt === 0 ||` is fully subsumed by the adjacent `elapsed >= throttleMs` condition and can never independently change the branch outcome. It is provably dead within the boolean and can be removed.
evidence: Line 142 computes `elapsed = now - state.lastProgressPublishedAt`. When `lastProgressPublishedAt === 0`, `elapsed = Date.now() - 0`, i.e. current epoch milliseconds (~1.75e12), which is always >= throttleMs (a few seconds at most, e.g. VISIBLE_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS = 1000). Therefore whenever the `=== 0` disjunct is true, `elapsed >= throttleMs` is already true, and the branch (immediate publishProgress) is taken regardless. Dropping `state.lastProgressPublishedAt === 0 ||` leaves behavior identical.
est_reduction: 1 sub-expression (~0 net lines; simplifies the throttle gate to a single comparison)
behavior_preservation: Identical: in every case where the removed disjunct is true the remaining comparison is also true, so the same publish-immediately branch is taken.
